item.title: President Lee Holds Kong-guksu Lunch with Blue House Staff for Chobok, Surprise Press Conference Also Held (李대통령, 초복 맞아 靑직원들과 콩국수 오찬…깜짝 기자간담회도)
item.description:
President Lee Holds Kong-guksu Lunch with Blue House Staff for Chobok, Surprise Press Conference Also Held (李대통령, 초복 맞아 靑직원들과 콩국수 오찬…깜짝 기자간담회도)

President Lee Jae-myung shared a "kong-guksu lunch" with staff at the Blue House cafeteria on the 15th to mark Chobok. After the lunch, he made a surprise visit to the Chunchugwan press room, where Blue House correspondents are stationed, and held a Q&A session for over an hour. <<> Blue House Senior Spokesperson Kang Yu-jung reported that eight staff members attended the lunch, including employees from heavy-duty departments such as the National Crisis Management Center, the Office of the Senior Secretary for Autonomy Development, and the Office of the Senior Secretary for Personnel, as well as outstanding staff who suggested policies for the Blue House. The menu for Chobok featured kong-guksu made with Korean wheat and Korean soybeans, along with baechu-jeon (cabbage pancakes), yeolmu-kimchi (young radish kimchi), and watermelon. <<> President Lee said via X (formerly Twitter) that day, "Thinking of our Blue House family, who silently fulfill their duties in their respective positions amidst various challenges big and small, I feel both sorry and reassured. I will do my best so that you can feel a full sense of pride and fulfillment in working at the Blue House, even though your work is busy and demanding." <<> After finishing the lunch, President Lee visited Chunchugwan without prior notice and held an informal meeting with Blue House reporters. During the one-hour-and-ten-minute session in Chunchugwan, the president discussed various national affairs with the reporters, holding a free Q&A session. (이재명 대통령이 15일 초복을 맞아 청와대 구내식당에서 직원들과 ‘콩국수 오찬’을 함께 했다. 오찬 후엔 청와대 출입기자들이 있는 춘추관에 깜짝 방문해 1시간 넘게 질의응답 시간을 가졌다.)

item.title: "Allies That Build Airports and Expand Welfare While Relying on U.S. Defense Must Realize the World Has Changed" (“美방어 의존하면서 공항 짓고, 복지 증진… 동맹, 세상 달라진 것 알아야”)
item.description:
"Allies That Build Airports and Expand Welfare While Relying on U.S. Defense Must Realize the World Has Changed" (“美방어 의존하면서 공항 짓고, 복지 증진… 동맹, 세상 달라진 것 알아야”)

Former U.S. Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice said on the 14th, "Allies who depend on U.S. defense while building great airports and constructing social welfare systems don't fully understand what's happening inside the United States." She added, "The U.S. is tired of shouldering the military burden alone. The world has changed, and (allied nations) must acknowledge that." Rice, the first female secretary of state under the George W. Bush administration, known as a hardliner on North Korea and nicknamed the "Iron Lady" in South Korea, made these remarks at the Aspen Security Forum (ASF) opening in Aspen, Colorado, stating, "I strongly support transatlantic and Asia-Pacific alliances, but the world has changed." (콘돌리자 라이스 전 국무장관은 14일 “미국의 방어에 의존하면서 훌륭한 공항을 짓고, 사회 복지 시스템을 건설하는 동맹이 미국 내 무슨 일이 벌어지고 있는지 제대로 이해하지 못하고 있다”며 “미국은 이제 홀로 군사적 부담을 짊어지는 데 지쳤다. 세상이 달라졌고 (동맹국도) 그 사실을 인정해야 한다”고 했다. 부시 정부에서 사상 첫 여성 장관을 지냈고, 대북 강경파이자 ‘철의 여인’이란 별명으로 국내에도 친숙한 라이스는 이날 콜로라도주(州) 애스펀에서 개막한 ‘애스펀안보포럼(ASF)’에 참석해 “대서양, 아시아·태평양 동맹을 강력히 지지하지만 세상이 달라졌다”며 이같이 밝혔다.)

Former Defense Secretary Mark Esper, who served during Trump's first term, also noted, "Trump accurately captured the voices of people who say, 'We're really fed up' with issues like national debt, student loans, and the cost of living." He added, "If other countries remain solely focused on their own welfare while endlessly expecting the status quo to continue, we cannot keep supporting global security." President Donald Trump, after returning to power, pressured NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organization) members to increase defense spending to 5% of their GDP, and Esper recalled that former President Barack Obama also emphasized the need to meet minimum standards and used the term "free riders" at the 2014 NATO summit. (트럼프 1기 때 국방장관을 지낸 마크 에스퍼도 “트럼프는 국가 부채, 학자금 대출, 생활비 부담 등으로 ‘이젠 정말 지긋지긋하다’는 국민들의 목소리를 제대로 포착한 것”이라며 “다른 나라들이 자국 복지 증진에만 몰두하면서 현재 상황이 계속되기를 끝없이 기대하면 우리가 계속해서 세계 안보를 지원해 줄 수는 없다”고 했다. 도널드 트럼프 대통령은 재집권 후 나토(NATO·북대서양조약기구) 회원국을 상대로 국방비를 국내총생산(GDP)의 5%까지 늘릴 것을 압박했는데, 에스퍼는 버락 오바마 전 대통령 역시 2014년 나토 회의 때 최저 기준 준수를 강조하며 ‘무임승차자’란 표현을 썼다고 했다.)

The rejection and criticism from Europe of the U.S.-led military operations against Iran, initiated by Trump, also came under scrutiny. Rice stated, "I love our allies, but it's not wise to say 'this isn't our war' while the U.S. is fighting." She argued, "Even if you don't participate in the war, you shouldn't try to hinder the effort; rather, you should support it." Rice expressed concern that some leaders' claims of "we can do it without the U.S." could fuel isolationists in the U.S. who advocate for disengaging from foreign affairs. Esper also criticized Spain, Italy, and others for refusing to use U.S. military bases, saying, "We only asked to use our bases, and it was really foolish." (트럼프가 시작한 대(對)이란 군사 작전 당시 유럽이 파병 요청을 거부하는 것을 넘어 이를 비판한 것도 도마 위에 올랐다. 라이스는 “동맹을 사랑하지만 미국이 싸우고 있는 상황에서 ‘이건 우리의 전쟁이 아니다’라고 말하는 건 현명한 일이 아니다”라고 했다. “설령 전쟁에 참여하지 않더라도 노력을 방해하려 해서는 안 되며 오히려 힘을 실어줘야 한다”는 것이다. 라이스는 ‘미국 없이도 우리가 해낼 수 있다’는 일부 정상의 주장이 대외 문제에서 손을 뗄 것을 주장해 온 미국 내 고립주의자들에 좋은 먹이감이 될 수 있다고 우려했다. 에스퍼 역시 스페인·이탈리아 등이 미군 기지 사용을 거부한 것을 언급하며 “단지 우리의 기지를 사용해달라고 요청했을 뿐인데 정말 어리석었다”고 비판했다.)

The Aspen Security Forum, which opened today, continues for four days until the 17th, with around 1,000 global opinion leaders in attendance. The forum stems from the Aspen Strategy Group (ASG), a bipartisan foreign policy and security discussion group founded by Harvard professor Joseph Nye, a former senior Democratic official and advocate of "soft power," and Brent Scowcroft, a former National Security Advisor under a Republican administration, who joined forces. The group started its public forum in 2010. In his opening remarks, former U.S. Ambassador to China Nicholas Burns, the forum's co-chair, quoted Nye, saying, "We all come here with strong opinions and will express them, but if we listen to others, we can learn something, and it's okay to change our minds." Unlike Rice and Esper, Burns said, "Without alliances like NATO, where would the U.S. be today?" (이날 개막한 애스펀안보포럼은 전 세계 오피니언 리더 약 1000명이 참석한 가운데, 17일까지 나흘 동안 계속된다. 1984년 민주당 정부 고위직을 지냈고 ‘소프트 파워’를 주창한 조셉 나이 하버드대 교수, 보수 정부에서 국가안보보좌관을 지낸 브렌트 스코크로프트가 의기투합해 초당적 외교·안보 토론 모임인 ‘애스펀전략그룹(ASG)’을 만들었고 2010년부터 공개 행사 성격의 포럼을 시작했다. 포럼 공동 의장으로 있는 니컬러스 번스 전 주중 대사는 개회사에서 “우리 모두 확고한 의견을 갖고 이곳에 왔고 그에 따라 의견을 개진하겠지만, 다른 사람의 말을 경청하면 무언가를 배울 수 있으며 생각을 바꾸는 것도 괜찮다”는 나이의 말을 인용했다. 라이스·에스퍼와 달리 번스는 “나토 같은 동맹이 없었다면 미국이 지금 어디 있었겠느냐”라고 했다.)

()

◇ ☞Aspen Institute (◇ ☞애스펀연구소(Aspen Institute))

The Aspen Institute is a nonprofit organization founded in 1949 in Aspen, Colorado, by American businessman Walter Paepcke. Inspired by Aspen's natural beauty, Paepcke, a Chicago native, conceived the idea of a gathering where global leaders could escape daily routines and engage in dialogue. Its mission is "to address the most important challenges facing the U.S. and the world through dialogue and leadership." It aims to serve as a nonpartisan convener, stepping back from political divides to bring together diverse participants for discussion. With over 30 independent programs covering fields like economics, education, and the environment, it has hosted the annual Aspen Security Forum since 2010, where global foreign policy and security experts discuss domestic and international issues. (미국의 사업가인 월터 펩키가 1949년 콜로라도주 애스펀에 설립한 비영리단체다. 시카고 출신으로 애스펀의 자연경관에 감동한 펩키가 세계의 리더들이 일상에서 벗어나 토론을 하는 아이디어를 구상한 것에서 비롯됐다. “대화와 리더십을 통해 미국과 전 세계가 직면한 가장 중요한 도전 과제들을 해결하겠다”는 것이 운영 취지다. 정치 구도에서 한 발짝 물러나 다양한 사람이 모여서 토론하도록 주선하는 초당적 주관자를 지향한다. 경제·교육·환경 등 30여 분야에서 각 프로그램이 독립적으로 운영되고 있는데, 2010년부터는 매년 전 세계 외교·안보 전문가들이 국내외 문제를 논의하는 ‘애스펀안보포럼’을 개최하고 있다.)

item.title: World Heritage Committee Tells Japan, Which Overlooks ‘Forced Labor of Koreans,’ to “Address the Full History” (세계유산위, ‘조선인 강제노동’ 외면 日에 “전체 역사 다뤄야”)
item.description:
World Heritage Committee Tells Japan, Which Overlooks ‘Forced Labor of Koreans,’ to “Address the Full History” (세계유산위, ‘조선인 강제노동’ 외면 日에 “전체 역사 다뤄야”)

The UNESCO World Heritage Committee recommended to Japan on the 15th that it must improve as the Japanese government has failed to properly disclose the fact that forced labor of Koreans occurred at the Sado Island Gold Mines. This recommendation calls for Japan to faithfully fulfill the promises it made when it inscribed the Sado Gold Mines as a World Heritage site in 2024. This recommendation is seen as bolstering the South Korean government's stance. (일본 정부가 사도광산에서 조선인 강제 노동이 이뤄진 사실을 제대로 알리지 않아 개선해야 한다고 유네스코 세계유산위원회가 15일 일본에 권고했다. 일본이 2024년 사도광산을 세계유산으로 등재할 당시 한 약속을 제대로 이행하라는 것이다. 이번 권고는 한국 정부의 입장에 힘을 실어준 것으로 평가된다.)

The World Heritage Committee conveyed this recommendation in a draft decision circulated to member states, based on its evaluation of the conservation status report (SOC) submitted by Japan regarding the Sado Gold Mines. The draft decision assessed that while Japan has made “some progress” in implementing the World Heritage Committee's recommendation to establish an interpretation and exhibition strategy reflecting the site’s “full history,” this progress is insufficient. (세계유산위는 이날 일본이 제출한 사도광산 보존현황보고서(SOC)를 평가한 결과 이같이 권고했다고 회원국에 회람한 결정문안에서 밝혔다. 결정문안은 사도광산의 ‘전체 역사’를 반영하는 해석·전시 전략을 수립하라는 세계유산위의 권고를 이행하는 데 있어서 일본 측의 “일부 진전”이 있었으나 충분하지 않다고 평가했다.)

The World Heritage Committee recommended that Japan “comprehensively address the full history of the mine over the entire period of its operation at the site level, and closely consult with the relevant State Parties to improve the interpretation and exhibition strategy and facilities at the site level.” A foreign ministry official explained that “full history” includes the history of Koreans being forced to labor in the mines by Japan during the Japanese colonial period. (세계유산위는 “광산 개발 모든 기간에 걸쳐 전체 역사를 현장 차원에서 포괄적으로 다루고, 현장 차원에서 해석·전시 전략 및 시설을 개선하기 위해 당사국들과 긴밀히 협의하라”고 권고했다. 여기서 ‘전체 역사’란 일제강점기 조선인이 일본에 의해 광산에서 강제로 노역한 역사를 포함한다고 외교부 당국자는 설명했다.)

While acknowledging the additional measures Japan has taken so far to implement the recommendation, the World Heritage Committee requested that Japan more clearly explain how its interpretation and exhibition strategy and facilities comprehensively cover the full history of the Sado Gold Mines and regularly report the relevant progress to the World Heritage Committee. (세계유산위는 일본이 권고 이행을 위해 그간 취한 추가 조치를 인정하면서도 일본의 해석·전시 전략과 시설이 어떻게 사도광산의 전체 역사를 포괄적으로 다루는지 더 명확히 설명하고, 관련 진전 사항을 세계유산위에 정기적으로 보고하라고 요청했다.)

The World Heritage Committee has asked Japan to submit a report on the implementation of this recommendation by December 1, 2027, and plans to review that implementation report at the 50th session of the World Heritage Committee to be held in 2028. (세계유산위는 일본에 이번 권고에 대한 이행 보고서를 2027년 12월 1일까지 제출하라고 했으며, 그 이행 보고서를 2028년에 열리는 제50차 세계유산위에서 검토할 계획이다.)

Meanwhile, the South Korean government has conveyed its position this year through two rounds of director-general-level bilateral consultations with Japan that the coercive nature of the labor involving Koreans in the interpretation and exhibition of the Sado Gold Mines must be expressed more clearly. It is known that this position has also been consistently explained to UNESCO. (그간 우리 정부는 일본에 사도광산 해석과 전시에 있어서 한국인이 참여한 노동의 강제성을 더 분명하게 표현해야 한다는 입장을 올해 두 차례의 한·일 국장급 대면 협의 등을 통해 전달했다. 이를 유네스코에도 지속해서 설명한 것으로 알려졌다.)

A foreign ministry official stated, “We see this as a reflection of our consistent position, given that Japan’s implementation of the related recommendations is insufficient,” and added, “We will continue to make necessary efforts while closely consulting with the UNESCO Secretariat and relevant countries to ensure that Japan faithfully implements the World Heritage Committee's decision and the promises made at the time of inscription.” (외교부 당국자는 “일본 측의 관련 권고 이행이 충분하지 않은 상황에서 우리 측의 일관된 입장이 반영된 것으로 본다”면서 “앞으로도 일본 측이 세계유산위원회 결정과 등재 당시 약속을 충실히 이행하도록 유네스코 사무국 및 관계국과 긴밀히 협의하면서 필요한 노력을 지속할 예정”이라고 말했다.)

This draft decision will be discussed as an agenda item at the 48th session of the World Heritage Committee taking place in Busan between the 20th and 23rd. It is expected to be adopted by consensus if there is no disagreement among member states. However, it remains uncertain how faithfully Japan will follow the recommendation, as there are no clear penalties for non-compliance. (이번 결정문안은 부산에서 열리는 제48차 세계유산위에서 20∼23일 사이 안건으로 논의되며, 위원국 간 이견이 없으면 합의로 채택될 전망이다. 다만 일본이 권고를 얼마나 따를지는 미지수다. 권고를 따르지 않는 데 대한 불이익이 분명하지 않기 때문이다.)

Japan has taken some limited measures. A foreign ministry official explained that while there were criticisms that access to facilities used by Korean workers at the Sado Gold Mines, such as dormitory sites or communal kitchens, was not easy, Japan installed about ten related signposts at the site in the first half of this year. (일본도 일부 제한적인 조치는 하고 있다. 사도광산은 기숙사 터나 공동 취사장 등 한국인 노동자가 사용한 시설을 찾아가기 쉽지 않다는 지적이 있었는데, 올해 상반기 일본은 현장에 관련 이정표 10여 개를 설치했다고 외교부 당국자는 설명했다.)

The Sado Gold Mines, once famous for gold, were primarily used as mines to secure war materials as the Pacific War intensified. During this period, colonial Koreans were forcibly mobilized, and it is known that 1,519 Koreans toiled at the Sado Gold Mines from 1940 to 1945. (금광으로 유명했던 사도광산은 태평양전쟁이 본격화하면서 전쟁 물자를 확보하는 광산으로 주로 이용됐다. 이때 식민지 조선인들이 강제 동원됐고, 1940∼1945년 사도광산에서 노역한 조선인은 1519명으로 알려졌다.)

The inscription of the Sado Gold Mines as a World Heritage site was decided at the 46th session of the World Heritage Committee held in New Delhi, India, in July 2024. Ahead of the inscription, the South Korean government demanded that the site reflect its “full history,” including the forced labor of Koreans, and Japan accepted this, but it has not been properly reflected to date. (사도광산은 2024년 7월 인도 뉴델리에서 열린 제46차 세계유산위에서 등재가 결정됐다. 등재를 앞두고 한국 정부는 사도광산에 조선인 강제 노동을 포함한 ‘전체 역사’를 반영해야 한다고 요구했고, 일본도 이를 수용했지만, 현재까지 제대로 반영되지 않고 있다.)

item.title: Jang Dong-hyuk heads to Gwangju after Incheon and Busan… Kwon Young-se “No one in our party knows what he’s doing” (인천·부산 이어 광주로 간 장동혁…권영세 “뭐하는지 우리 당은 아무도 몰라”)
item.description:
Jang Dong-hyuk heads to Gwangju after Incheon and Busan… Kwon Young-se “No one in our party knows what he’s doing” (인천·부산 이어 광주로 간 장동혁…권영세 “뭐하는지 우리 당은 아무도 몰라”)

People Power Party (PPP) leader Jang Dong-hyuk attended a rally on the evening of the 15th in front of the Gwangju Election Commission in South Jeolla Province, protesting the shortage of ballot papers in the June 3 local elections. This marked his third local rally schedule, following visits to Incheon and Busan. Chairman Jang is also attending a rally at Olympic Park in Songpa-gu, Seoul, in a personal capacity. Within the party, there are reactions saying, “While we must protect voting rights through a special counsel investigation into the Election Commission, it’s hard to understand continuing personal schedules like this outside the National Assembly rather than inside it.” <<> At the rally that day, Chairman Jang stated, “I am willing to stake my political life on protecting the precious vote of the people.” He added, “I hope we can gather at Olympic Park on July 17 (Constitution Day) and show together how hot our anger is and how great our patriotism is,” in the sense of making it a day to restore constitutional order in South Korea by recovering voting rights. <<> In a Pen & Mike YouTube interview before attending the rally, Chairman Jang also said, “If by Constitution Day, negotiations on forming the (parliamentary) leadership and the special counsel for the Election Commission are not conducted in a way we find acceptable, I will not attend this Constitution Day event,” encouraging participation in the Olympic Park rally. Regarding the issue of reinstating independent lawmaker Han Dong-hoon (Busan North Gap) into the party, Jang said, “He remains as someone who prevented martial law and led the impeachment, but to push Choo Kyung-ho (Daegu Mayor) and the PPP into a corner and then suddenly say he wants to rejoin the PPP—what kind of logic is that?” <<> Amid Chairman Jang’s continued outside activities, five-term lawmaker Kwon Young-se (Seoul Yongsan) said, “Regardless of how the leadership system changes later, Chairman Jang needs to resign.” Appearing on CBS Radio, Kwon stated, “If he were thinking about how to change the party, there might be a reason to stay, but he shows no such consideration, is completely fixated on voting rights issues, and only operates outside the party. He should aim for conservative victory, but he promotes personal ambition like ‘I must be the front-runner’ and puts private greed and self-interest ahead, sacrificing the party or conservative forces.” <<> Supreme Council member Jo Kwang-han, a close aide to Chairman Jang, told reporters that day, referring to Kwon Young-se, “Isn’t he the one who brought up the idea of nominating Han Deok-soo during the last presidential election and caused tremendous chaos late at night? He has no right to say such things.” <<> Meanwhile, Chairman Jang attended a ‘June 3 Local Election Evaluation and Analysis Meeting’ hosted by ‘Good Friend (GF),’ a gathering of non-incumbent district party chairpersons, held in Indeokwon, Anyang, Gyeonggi Province on the 12th. Regarding this gathering, some within the party speculated, “Isn’t this a venue for Chairman Jang to boost the chances of his close aide, Supreme Council member Jo Kwang-han, in his bid for Gyeonggi Province party chairperson?” <<> Good Friend is a policy study group involving about 50 non-incumbent district party chairpersons from the PPP. The meeting was reportedly attended by Party Leader’s Chief of Staff, lawmaker Park Joon-tae, Supreme Council member Jo Kwang-han, and about 20 non-incumbent district party chairpersons from the Seoul metropolitan area. <<> Among the attendees were district party chairpersons including Oh Kyung-hoon (Seoul Yangcheon B), Jang Sung-ho (Guro B), Kwon Soon-young (Goyang Gap, Gyeonggi), Shin Young-rak (Hwaseong B), Han Gil-ryong (Paju B), Ahn Ki-young (Yangju), Hong Yoon-oh (Suwon B), Kwak Nae-kyung (Bucheon Gap), Seo Young-seok (Bucheon B), Ko Seok (Yongin C), Lee Joo-hyun (Yongin F), Lee Bong-joon (Suwon Gap), Lee Soo-jung (Suwon D), Park Jae-soon (Suwon F), Yoo Young-doo (Gwangju Gap, Gyeonggi), Jeon Dong-seok (Gwangmyeong B), Park Jong-jin (Incheon Yeonsu Gap), Son Beom-gyu (Namdong Gap), and Park Kyung-ho (Daejeon Daedeok). (국민의힘 장동혁 대표가 15일 저녁 전남광주 선관위 앞에서 열린 6·3 지방선거 투표용지 부족 사태 규탄 집회에 참석했다. 인천, 부산에 이어 세 번째 지방 집회 일정이다. 장 대표는 서울 송파구 올림픽공원에서 열리는 집회에도 개인 자격으로 참석하고 있다. 당내에선 “선관위 특검을 통해 참정권 수호를 관철해야 하지만 국회가 아니라 장외에서 이런 식의 개인 일정을 이어가는 것은 이해할 수 없다”는 반응도 나온다.)

item.title: Lee: “Kim Yong’s Ruling Hard to Understand” ... Inside Party: “A Message to Vote for Him” (李 “김용 판결 이해 어렵다”... 당내 “표 주라는 메시지”)
item.description:
Lee: “Kim Yong’s Ruling Hard to Understand” ... Inside Party: “A Message to Vote for Him” (李 “김용 판결 이해 어렵다”... 당내 “표 주라는 메시지”)

President Lee Jae-myung on the 15th referred to the bribery case involving Kim Yong, former deputy director of the Democratic Party Research Institute who ran for the party’s Supreme Council, and said of the court ruling that found the former deputy director guilty, “It is truly hard to understand.” President Lee had previously remarked about Kim Yong, “He should be at least on the level of Kim Yong to be considered a close associate.” Within the party, there were reactions such as, “Isn’t the President effectively signaling support for the former deputy director in the Supreme Council election?” (이재명 대통령은 15일 더불어민주당 최고위원에 출마한 김용 전 민주연구원 부원장의 뇌물 수수 혐의 사건을 언급하면서, 김 전 부원장에게 유죄를 선고한 법원 판결에 대해 “참으로 이해하기 어렵다”고 했다. 이 대통령은 과거 김 전 부원장에 대해 “김용 정도는 돼야 측근”이라고 했었다. 당내에서는 “대통령이 최고위원 선거에서 사실상 김 전 부원장을 지지해 달라는 신호를 보낸 것 아니냐”는 반응이 나왔다.)

President Lee shared a post by Democratic Party lawmaker Lee Geon-tae on X (formerly Twitter) that afternoon, criticizing the court ruling against former deputy director Kim. Earlier, Kim was found guilty of receiving 670 million won in illegal political funds and bribes from private developers in the Daejang-dong case, receiving a five-year prison sentence and a 70 million won fine in both the first and second trials, with a Supreme Court ruling pending. Kim’s side argued that ‘Google Timeline,’ which records location information, showed he was not at the location where prosecutors claimed the money was received, but the court did not accept this. <<> In his post on X that day, Lawmaker Lee argued that prosecutors intentionally ignored Google Timeline while investigating and indicting Kim. He claimed that prosecutors actively used Google Timeline as evidence in other cases but did not do so in Kim’s case, calling it a “double standard by the prosecution.” <<> Citing Lee’s post, President Lee said, “It is truly hard to understand how Google Timeline, which has been used in court as evidence of guilt, is only in certain cases deemed insufficient as evidence of innocence, leading to the bizarre conclusion that even though Google Timeline proves an alibi, the accused is still indicted and convicted.” This indicated his agreement with the lawmaker’s argument. <<> President Lee’s post on X drew reactions within the Democratic Party such as, “This is a message from President Lee to party members to cast votes for former deputy director Kim.” Since Kim is expected to be incarcerated if the Supreme Court confirms his conviction, even among Democratic Party supporters, there have been questions like, “Is it right to vote for him?” Some also questioned whether it was problematic for the President to post what seemed like a message supporting Kim, a pro-Lee candidate, during the party convention, which is unfolding as a pro-Lee vs. pro-Chung conflict. (이 대통령은 이날 오후 X(옛 트위터)에 김 전 부원장의 법원 판결을 비판한 이건태 민주당 의원의 글을 공유했다. 앞서 김 전 부원장은 대장동 민간 업자들로부터 불법 정치자금과 뇌물 6억7000만원을 받은 혐의가 인정돼 1·2심에서 징역 5년과 벌금 7000만원을 선고받고, 대법원 판결을 앞두고 있다. 김 전 부원장 측은 위치 정보가 기록된 ‘구글 타임라인’을 근거로 검찰이 돈을 받았다고 지목한 장소에 있지 않았다고 주장했지만 법원에서 받아들여지지 않았다.)

item.title: Voices within the Ruling Party Also Spread, Calling for "Retention of Supplementary Investigation Authority" (與서도 “보완수사권 유지” 목소리 확산)
item.description:
Voices within the Ruling Party Also Spread, Calling for "Retention of Supplementary Investigation Authority" (與서도 “보완수사권 유지” 목소리 확산)

Within the Democratic Party of Korea, voices opposing the complete abolition of prosecutors' supplementary investigation authority are growing louder. Some lawmakers are even considering proposing legislation that would allow supplementary investigation authority in cases such as digital sex crimes. (더불어민주당 내에서 검사의 보완수사권 전면 폐지에 반대하는 목소리가 커지고 있다. 일부 의원은 디지털 성범죄 등 사건에 보완수사권을 허용하는 법안을 발의하는 방안도 검토하고 있다.)

Former Minister of Justice Park Beom-kye, speaking at a general meeting of Democratic Party lawmakers on the 14th, reportedly argued that without prosecutors' supplementary investigation authority, gaps could arise in cases where the detention period or statute of limitations is about to expire, or for crimes requiring swift investigation due to the ease of destroying evidence. Three-term lawmaker Maeng Seong-gyu also expressed the opinion that supplementary investigation authority should be exceptionally retained for sex crimes and crimes against children, adolescents, the disabled, and the elderly. Both lawmakers are considering proposing amendments to the Criminal Procedure Act containing such provisions. Previously, 11 Democratic Party lawmakers, including Rep. Hong Gi-won, proposed a revision to the Criminal Procedure Act to retain prosecutors' supplementary investigation authority for crimes against social minorities or for everyday crimes like voice phishing. (법무부 장관을 지낸 박범계 의원은 지난 14일 민주당 의원총회에 참석해 구속기한이나 공소시효 만료가 임박했거나, 증거 삭제가 쉬워 신속한 수사가 필요한 범죄의 경우 검사의 보완수사권이 없을 때 공백이 발생할 수 있다고 주장했다고 한다. 3선인 맹성규 의원도 성폭력 범죄와 아동·청소년·장애인·노인 대상 범죄는 예외적으로 보완수사권을 유지하자는 의견을 냈다. 두 의원은 이런 내용을 담은 형사소송법 개정안을 발의하는 방안도 검토하고 있다. 앞서 홍기원 의원 등 민주당 의원 11명은 사회적 약자를 대상으로 하거나, 보이스피싱 등 민생 범죄에 대해서는 검사의 보완수사권을 유지하도록 하는 내용의 형소법 개정안을 발의했다.)

Their claims differ from the Democratic Party's task force (TF) proposal for amending the Criminal Procedure Act, which would completely abolish the supplementary investigation authority and only grant the authority to request supplementary investigations. Minister of Justice Jeong Seong-ho stated at the National Assembly's Legislation and Judiciary Committee that day, "If we assume abolition of supplementary investigation, we must ensure there are no victims among the 1% who might suffer unfairly." (이들의 주장은 검사의 보완수사권을 완전 폐지하고 보완수사 요구권만 부여하는 민주당 형소법 개정 태스크포스(TF) 안과는 차이가 있다. 정성호 법무부 장관은 이날 국회 법제사법위원회에서 “보완수사 폐지를 전제로 한다고 하면 억울한 1%의 피해자가 없도록 해야 한다“고 했다.)

Following lawyers' groups and women's organizations, victims of violent crimes also opposed the complete abolition of supplementary investigation authority. Victims of incidents such as the "Busan roundhouse kick case" held a press conference at the Seoul Seocho-gu Bar Association building that day, arguing, "The current prosecution reform is being carried out with victims excluded," and insisting that "victim protection measures must be established first." (변호사 단체, 여성단체에 이어 강력범죄 피해자들도 보완수사권 전면 폐지에 반대했다. ‘부산 돌려차기 사건’ 등 피해자들은 이날 서울 서초구 변호사회관에서 기자회견을 열고 “지금의 검찰개혁은 피해자가 배제된 채 이뤄지고 있다”며 “피해자 보호 장치를 먼저 마련해야 한다”고 주장했다.)

Within the Democratic Party, the possibility of delaying the handling of the Criminal Procedure Act is also being discussed. The party initially aimed to finalize the revision of the Criminal Procedure Act before the August 17 party convention, which will elect the next party leader. A lawmaker from the party's leadership said, "We need to fully heed the opinions that supplementary investigation authority should be exceptionally retained," adding, "Although it's difficult to fix a timeline for processing, we are also keeping in mind the possibility that discussions may continue after the party convention." (민주당 내부에서는 형소법 처리 시점이 늦춰질 가능성도 거론된다. 민주당은 애초 차기 당대표를 뽑는 8·17 전당대회 이전에 형소법 개정을 마무리하겠다는 입장이었다. 민주당 지도부의 한 의원은 “예외적으로 보완수사권을 존치해야 한다는 의견을 충분히 들을 필요가 있다”며 “처리 시점을 못 박기는 어렵지만 전당대회 이후로 논의가 이어질 가능성도 염두에 두고 있다”고 했다.)

item.title: "If You Let Them Off, You'll Be Screwed": The Deep-Rooted Distrust of the Prosecution Among the Hardline Faction of the Ruling Party (“봐주면 당한다” 與강경파의 뿌리 깊은 검찰 불신)
item.description:
"If You Let Them Off, You'll Be Screwed": The Deep-Rooted Distrust of the Prosecution Among the Hardline Faction of the Ruling Party (“봐주면 당한다” 與강경파의 뿌리 깊은 검찰 불신)

On the 15th, hardliners from the Democratic Party of Korea directed harsh criticism at party lawmakers who opposed the complete abolition of supplementary investigative powers, saying, "Why are you arbitrarily overturning the party line?" and "You are committing a grave sin before history." They emphasized that now is the time to achieve what was left unfinished during the Moon Jae-in administration—the so-called "complete stripping of prosecution investigative powers." (더불어민주당 강경파는 15일 당내 보완수사권 완전 폐지 반대 목소리를 내는 의원들을 향해 “왜 마음대로 당론을 뒤집냐” “역사 앞에 큰 죄를 짓는 것”이라고 했다. 이들은 이번에야말로 문재인 정부 때 이루지 못했던 이른바 ‘검수완박(검찰 수사권 완전 박탈)’을 해야 할 때라고 강조하고 있다.)

Jeong Cheong-rae, a former party leader who was at the forefront of prosecution reform, wrote on Facebook as calls grew within the Democratic Party to partially retain supplementary investigative powers: "This is really serious. Why has this atmosphere suddenly emerged? I'm depressed." Jeong had repeatedly stated during his tenure as party leader that "abolition is the party line." (검찰 개편 관련 가장 선봉에 섰던 정청래 전 대표는 민주당 내 보완수사권 일부 존치 주장에 커지자 페이스북에 “정말 심각하다. 갑자기 왜 이런 분위기가 됐는지. 우울하다”고 썼다. 정 전 대표는 당대표 시절 ”폐지가 당론”이라고 여러차례 말한 바 있다.)

Pro-Jeong faction Supreme Council member Moon Jeong-bok also said on the same day, "Prosecution reform is a generational task that party members and the people have commanded of the Democratic Party." He added, "If this is shaken or derailed again by conflicting interests and claims within the party, the Democratic Party will bear great responsibility before history." He further argued, "The abolition of supplementary investigative powers is already a clear party line that the Democratic Party has announced to its members and the people." This was in reaction to the party having set the policy of "abolishing supplementary investigative powers while retaining the right to request supplemental investigations" as party line in February, only for some to now claim it "was not the party line." Lawmaker Choi Min-hee also expressed concern, saying, "With a leader who has a strong will for prosecution reform, I'm very worried that various requests that used to fail are now getting through to the Democratic Party." <<> The hardline support base of the ruling party harbors a deep-seated distrust of the prosecution. Their view is that the Roh Moo-hyun and Moon Jae-in administrations were undermined by a politicized prosecution, leading to the failure of those governments. In particular, they assess that the failure to complete the stripping of prosecution investigative powers during the Moon administration led to the 'Cho Kuk incident,' which in turn resulted in the birth of the Yoon Suk Yeol government and even martial law. President Lee Jae-myung is also seen as a victim of fabricated prosecutorial investigations. On the bulletin board of Kim Eo-joon's Ddanji Ilbo, a hub for hardline supporters, posts have poured in saying things like, "If this continues, the prosecution will get us again," "If President Lee Jae-myung joins hands with the prosecution like this, he's unforgivable," and "Lee Jae-myung is a traitor to the democratic camp." (친청(친정청래)계 문정복 최고위원도 이날 “검찰개혁은 당원과 국민이 민주당에 명령한 시대적 과제“라면서 “이를 당내의 엇갈린 이해와 주장으로 다시 흔들거나 좌초시킨다면 민주당은 역사 앞에 큰 책임을 지게 될 것”이라고 했다. 이어 “보완수사권 폐지는 이미 민주당이 당원과 국민 앞에 밝힌 분명한 당론”이라고 했다. 당이 지난 2월 당론으로 ‘보완수사권 폐지, 보완수사요구권 유지’를 정해놓고 이제와서 ”당론이 아니었다“고 했다며 반발한 것이다. 최민희 의원도 “검찰개혁에 강력한 의지를 가진 대표가 있어서 통하지 않던 각종 부탁이 민주당에 통하고 있나 싶어 무척 걱정된다”고 했다.)

item.title: Democratic Party Leadership Steps Back… Han Byeong-do: "Will Go Through Sufficient Deliberation" (한발 물러선 與지도부… 한병도 “충분한 숙의 거칠 것”)
item.description:
Democratic Party Leadership Steps Back… Han Byeong-do: "Will Go Through Sufficient Deliberation" (한발 물러선 與지도부… 한병도 “충분한 숙의 거칠 것”)

Within the Democratic Party of Korea, the argument that the prosecution's supplementary investigation authority should be partially retained is growing louder. The party leadership also appears to have stepped back, stating, "We will go through a sufficient deliberation process." (더불어민주당에서 검찰 보완수사권을 일부 남겨야 한다는 주장이 더 커지고 있다. 당 지도부도 “충분한 숙의 과정을 거치겠다”며 한발 물러선 모양새다.)

Acting Party Leader and Floor Leader Han Byeong-do said at the party's supreme council meeting that day, "We will continue deliberation while gathering opinions from the legal community, academia, and civil society," adding, "We will catch both rabbits—deliberation and timely legislation." This comes after 10 out of 15 lawmakers who spoke at the general meeting of lawmakers the previous day expressed concerns over complete abolition, indicating that the deliberation process for the revision of the Criminal Procedure Act to abolish the supplementary investigation authority will be further extended. A party official said, "The goal was to pass it in the plenary session of the National Assembly before the August 17 party convention, but there could be further discussions on the timing." <<> Five-term lawmaker Park Ji-won, who had until recently insisted on the complete abolition of the supplementary investigation authority, also changed his stance. Park had previously said to moderates within the party, "Are you not going to make jang (soybean paste) because you're afraid of maggots?" but on this day, he appeared on the radio and said, "It's not our opinion that matters, but the people's thoughts." He added, "For crimes against the socially disadvantaged, such as youth, women, and the disabled, it is right to have the supplementary investigation authority." <<> Lawmaker Lee So-young, who co-sponsored lawmaker Hong Gi-won's bill to partially retain the supplementary investigation authority, said in a CBS radio interview targeting hardliners, "If you can't clearly explain why the complete abolition of the supplementary investigation authority is the completion of prosecution reform, that's incitement." She also argued, "Unrelated investigations, targeted investigations, and covering up cases involving those in power are not related to granting the supplementary investigation authority," adding, "Unrelated and targeted investigations are already not possible, and covering up cases for the powerful—if a case comes to the prosecution with insufficient evidence—abolishing the supplementary investigation authority would actually create a better environment for dropping charges by blaming the police." <<> Lawmaker Kim Nam-hee, who also co-sponsored the bill, said on SBS radio, criticizing hardliners, "They talk about the abolition of the supplementary investigation authority as if it's an absolute truth and use it as a tool to appeal to hardline party members," calling it "a highly inappropriate act for a politician." <<> The presidential office has not yet stated a clear position on the supplementary investigation authority issue, where disagreements within the ruling party are erupting. Until now, President Yoon had called for partially retaining the supplementary investigation authority or preparing proper supplementary measures. However, amid recent backlash from hardline supporters, he reportedly said, "The National Assembly must decide and also take responsibility." A Democratic Party lawmaker commented, "Aren't the lawmakers who co-sponsored the retention bill mostly pro-Moon?" adding, "The content of the bill also resembles the government's original plan, which mirrored the president's thinking." (한병도 당대표 직무대행 겸 원내대표는 이날 당 최고위에서 “법조계와 학계, 시민사회의 의견을 수렴하면서 숙의를 이어가겠다”며 “숙의와 적기 입법이라는 두 마리 토끼를 모두 잡겠다”고 했다. 전날 의원총회에서 발언한 15명 가운데 10명이 완전 폐지를 우려하는 의견을 내자, 보완수사권 폐지를 위한 형사소송법 개정안에 대한 숙의 과정을 더 거치겠다는 것이다. 민주당 관계자는 “8·17 전당대회 전 국회 본회의 처리가 목표였지만, 시점에 대한 재논의도 있을 수 있다”고 했다.)

item.title: 'Further extension of comprehensive special counsel' passes judiciary committee solely by ruling party (‘종합특검 재차 연장’ 與단독 법사위 통과)
item.description:
'Further extension of comprehensive special counsel' passes judiciary committee solely by ruling party (‘종합특검 재차 연장’ 與단독 법사위 통과)

The National Assembly's Legislation and Judiciary Committee held a plenary session on the 15th and passed a revision to the special counsel law, led by the Democratic Party of Korea, to increase the personnel of the second comprehensive special counsel (Special Counsel Kwon Chang-young) from 130 to 150 and extend the investigation period by one month. The People Power Party did not attend. (국회 법제사법위원회가 15일 전체회의를 열고 2차종합특검(특별검사 권창영)의 인력을 130명에서 150명으로 늘리고, 수사기간을 1개월 연장하는 특검법 개정안을 더불어민주당 주도로 의결했다. 국민의힘은 불참했다.)

The second comprehensive special counsel is tasked with investigating areas where the three major special counsel investigations—into insurrection, Kim Keon-hee, and the Marine's death in the line of duty—were insufficient, as well as newly raised allegations. It was launched in February and was scheduled to conclude its activities on the 24th. The People Power Party stated, "From the first three major special counsels to this one, the total activity period of the special counsel amounts to 690 days," and called it "a permanent establishment of a special counsel tailored to the ruling party's tastes." (2차종합특검은 내란·김건희·순직해병 등 3대 특검 수사에서 미진한 부분과 새롭게 제기된 의혹을 수사하는 특검이다. 지난 2월 출범해 오는 24일 활동을 종료할 예정이었다. 국민의힘은 “1차 3대 특검부터 이번까지 특검 활동 기간만 690일”이라며 “여당 입맛에 맞는 특검을 상설화하는 것”이라고 했다.)

The revision increases the quota for public officials dispatched to the special counsel from 130 to 150 and adds the Ministry of National Defense to the list of agencies that can be requested for dispatch. It also includes provisions for appointing attorneys with over five years of legal experience among special investigators to handle the maintenance of prosecution—managing court proceedings for cases indicted by the special counsel. Additionally, it stipulates that the second comprehensive special counsel must consult with the existing three major special counsels on matters that could overturn their decisions or affect the maintenance of indictments. (개정안은 특검 파견 공무원 정원을 130명에서 150명으로 늘리고, 파견 요청 기관에 국방부를 추가했다. 법조 경력 5년 이상인 특별수사관 가운데 공소유지 변호사를 지정해 특검이 기소한 사건의 공판 진행을 맡도록 하는 내용도 담겼다. 2차종합특검이 기존 3대 특검의 결정을 번복하거나 공소 유지에 영향을 줄 수 있는 사안은 해당 특검과 협의하도록 했다.)

The revision also adds 'obstruction of audit' to the scope of the special counsel's investigation. The special counsel is currently investigating suspicions surrounding the relocation of former President Yoon Seok-yeol's office and residence, while the Democratic Party has argued that the Board of Audit and Inspection previously downsized and covered up the case through negligent audits. Legal circles have pointed out that the special counsel may have begun investigating the audit agency's case first and then supplemented the legal basis through this legislative amendment. (개정안은 특검 수사 대상에 ‘감사 방해’를 추가했다. 특검은 윤석열 전 대통령 집무실·관저 이전 의혹을 수사 중인데, 민주당은 그간 당시 감사원이 부실 감사를 통해 사건을 축소·은폐했다고 주장해왔다. 법조계에선 특검이 감사원 사건에 대해 먼저 수사를 시작해 놓고 법 개정으로 근거를 보완한 것 아니냐는 지적이 나오고 있다.)

People Power Party floor leader Jeong Jeom-sik said, "The combined total is 690 days: 510 days for the first three major special counsel investigations, 150 days for the second comprehensive special counsel, and an additional 30 days for this extension," questioning, "Is it normal for a special counsel to operate for two years?" The People Power Party noted that a budget of 37 billion won has been allocated for the three major special counsels from last year through to the second comprehensive special counsel. Senior spokesperson Park Seong-hun issued a statement saying, "The special counsel is a temporary and exceptional system that operates only within the period set by law," and argued that "changing the rules mid-game, like a referee, because the investigation has not proceeded as desired or yielded the expected conclusion, is a frontal challenge to the rule of law." (국민의힘 정점식 원내대표는 “1차 3대 특검 수사 기간 510일과 2차종합특검 수사 기간 150일, 이번 추가 연장 30일을 합하면 모두 690일”이라며 “특검이 2년씩 가동되는 것이 정상적이냐”고 했다. 국민의힘은 작년 3대 특검에 이어 2차종합특검까지 370억원 예산이 투입됐다고 지적했다. 박성훈 수석대변인은 논평을 내고 “특검은 법이 정한 기간 안에서만 운영되는 한시적, 예외적 제도”라며 “수사가 뜻대로 되지 않고 원하는 결론을 얻지 못했다고 경기 도중 심판이 규칙 바꾸듯 법을 고치는 것은 법치주의에 대한 정면 도전”이라고 했다)

The Democratic Party has stated its intention to hold a plenary session of the National Assembly before the 24th of this month, the end date of the second comprehensive special counsel, and process the extension of the special counsel. (민주당은 2차종합특검 종료일인 이달 24일 이전에 국회 본회의를 열고 특검 연장안을 처리하겠다는 입장이다.)

item.title: Will the "Sea Cadet Without a Sea" and "Air Cadet Without a Runway" Become a Reality? (바다 없는 海士, 활주로 없는 空士 현실화되나)
item.description:
Will the "Sea Cadet Without a Sea" and "Air Cadet Without a Runway" Become a Reality? (바다 없는 海士, 활주로 없는 空士 현실화되나)

The Ministry of National Defense is reportedly strongly considering a plan to integrate the Army, Navy, and Air Force academies, allowing all cadets to complete their 1st through 4th year programs together at Jaundae (Purple Cloud Base) in Daejeon. The government and the ruling party are expected to review and announce a basic plan for establishing a "National Military Academy" containing these details during a party-government consultation on the 16th. <<> According to a comprehensive report by this newspaper on the 15th, the Ministry of National Defense is known to be actively reviewing a plan to merge the Army, Navy, and Air Force academies and establish a four-year National Military Academy at Jaundae in Daejeon. Jaundae, located in the Jaun-dong, Sinbong-dong, and Chumok-dong areas of Yuseong-gu, Daejeon, currently houses field-grade officer training facilities for each service and covers an area of 5.55 million square meters (approximately 1.68 million pyeong). A military source said, "I understand that the Army Logistics School site in Jaundae is spacious and is being strongly considered by the Defense Ministry as a candidate location for the National Military Academy," adding, "I heard that a high-ranking Defense Ministry official has already conducted an on-site inspection." Until the National Military Academy facilities are established in Jaundae, there is a possibility of temporarily using the Army Academy in Nowon-gu, Seoul. <<> Within the military, there are criticisms that merging the three academies into one at Jaundae would result in "a naval academy without a sea and an air force academy without a runway." The Ministry of National Defense is reportedly planning to adopt a "2+2 system," where 1st and 2nd-year cadets receive common basic education, while 3rd and 4th-year cadets are divided by service (Army, Navy, Air Force) for specialized training. It is said that the goal is for 3rd and 4th-year cadets to also continue their education at Jaundae. Previously, it was reported that the Army would train 3rd and 4th-year cadets in Jangseong, South Jeolla Province; the Navy in Jinhae, South Gyeongsang Province; and the Air Force in Cheongju, North Chungcheong Province. <<> The current Naval Academy in Jinhae-gu, Changwon, South Gyeongsang Province, is adjacent to the Jinhae Naval Base. The Air Force Academy in Cheongju, North Chungcheong Province, has the Air Force Aerospace Medical Center on its grounds, enabling flight environment adaptation training, and a flight training unit (the 212th Flight Squadron) and runway are located approximately 2 kilometers in a straight line from the academy. Specialized aerospace engineering research facilities, such as a wind tunnel laboratory and an astronomical observatory, are also within the Air Force Academy grounds. However, concerns are being raised that without a sea or runway near Jaundae in Daejeon, specialized Navy and Air Force training would not be feasible. <<> The Ministry of National Defense is reportedly of the view that Navy and Air Force practical training is concentrated during specific periods, so cadets can simply move and train during those times. Currently, the Naval Academy conducts a one-week summer combat swimming course and a four-week summer military practice session at sea for all 1st to 4th-year cadets, and it is argued that there is no problem if they leave Jaundae only during the summer. Similarly, the Air Force Academy's introductory flight education course, which requires a runway, is reportedly conducted for a few months during the 4th year. <<> However, a military source questioned, "Can the character of an officer who nurtures their dreams from enrollment in a fully equipped environment be the same as someone who only goes out for a few weeks of practical training?" A Ministry of National Defense official stated, "The Ministry will soon provide a detailed explanation of the basic plan for establishing a world-class military academy to foster elite officers capable of leading future warfare. We plan to refine the plan through public opinion-gathering processes such as public hearings and policy briefings." <<> Earlier, the Academy Reform Committee under the Ministry of National Defense's public-private-military joint special advisory committee proposed that the integrated education for 1st and 2nd-year cadets should take place at the Army Academy in Seoul. This was based on the view that the declining admission scores of the Naval and Air Force academies are partly influenced by their locations, suggesting that staying in Seoul would be advantageous for attracting top talent and faculty. <<> Nevertheless, the selection of Daejeon's Jaundae as the site for the National Military Academy is interpreted as reflecting the current government's policy of balanced regional development. A retired Army general said, "I wonder if they initially floated the idea of moving the Army Academy to Jangseong, South Jeolla, but then announced Jaundae in Daejeon, which is closer to Seoul, hoping to somewhat reduce opposition from those against the merger of the academies." While the integration of the Army, Navy, and Air Force academies was a campaign promise of President Lee Jae-myung, the alumni associations of all three academies are opposed to it. (국방부가 육·해·공군 사관학교를 통합해 모든 생도가 대전 자운대(紫雲臺)에서 1~4학년 과정을 함께 밟는 안을 유력 검토하고 있는 것으로 알려졌다. 정부와 여당은 16일 당정 협의를 열어 이런 내용을 포함한 ‘국군사관학교’ 창설 기본계획을 검토한 뒤 발표할 예정이다.)

item.title: Yoo Si-min: "Lee's Misguided Judgment, Heading Down an Inevitable Path to Failure" (유시민 “李 잘못된 판단, 필연적 실패의 길로 가고 있다”)
item.description:
Yoo Si-min: "Lee's Misguided Judgment, Heading Down an Inevitable Path to Failure" (유시민 “李 잘못된 판단, 필연적 실패의 길로 가고 있다”)

On the 15th, Yoo Si-min criticized President Lee Jae-myung's "prosecution reform" and management of state affairs, stating that he "is making a very misguided judgment" and "heading down an inevitable path to failure." It is unusual for a ruling camp figure to publicly criticize the administration by mentioning "failure" just as the Lee Jae-myung government has entered its second year in office. Amid the abolition of the prosecution's supplementary investigation power and the upcoming August Democratic Party of Korea national convention, there are also predictions that factional conflicts within the ruling camp could escalate into an internal civil war. <<> Yoo appeared on the pro-government YouTube channel "Maebul Show" that day and said, "The reason prosecution reform has not been achieved for over a year is because the President does not want a complete separation of investigation and indictment." President Lee had previously mentioned the need for the prosecution's supplementary investigation power in exceptional cases. However, under pressure from the ruling party's hardline supporters, then-Prime Minister Kim Min-seok announced last month the principle of abolishing the supplementary investigation power and delegated legislation to the Democratic Party. <<> Yoo said, "Even now, some lawmakers have proposed amendments that preserve part of (the supplementary investigation power), leaving some investigative authority with the prosecution," adding, "It's because they know the President's thoughts." He continued, "(The President) should have handled this responsibly. (But) he had the Justice Minister handle it, had the Prime Minister handle it, and so on," and added, "Delegating the dirty work to those below is straight out of Machiavelli's 'The Prince'." <<> Regarding the Democratic Party's national convention, he said, "(President Lee) didn't say 'Jung Cheong-rae, don't run,' but he has repeatedly promoted Prime Minister Kim Min-seok on social media beyond just kind words," and "This isn't a legal issue, but politically it should not be done." Referring to the party leader candidate and the Democratic Party's Seoul mayoral candidate, he said, "We must prevent 'Myung-pick' (President Lee's choice) from happening, but he has intervened in that way quite a bit." He added, "The Democratic Party should not be dominated by the President. The moment it accepts domination by a president with power, the party will disintegrate." <<> Yoo claimed that President Lee is trying to change the structure of the Democratic Party, saying, "We expected an extension, but the President seems to be thinking of reconstruction or redevelopment," and argued, "With the current approach, there is a very high possibility of ending in a disastrous outcome where the President gets hurt, the Democratic Party is ruined, and the camp is shattered." This is interpreted as a remark targeting President Lee and the pro-Lee faction within the party. Yoo has been seen as representing the pro-Roh (pro-Roh Moo-hyun) and pro-Moon (pro-Moon Jae-in) factions within the ruling camp. <<> In response to Yoo's remarks, Democratic Party lawmaker Jang Chul-min, a pro-Lee figure, said, "He crossed the line. How can a mouth that once called him a comrade spew such curses?" Another pro-Lee lawmaker, Lee Geon-tae, said, "It's more than shocking; it's irresponsible," and added, "What will inevitably fail is Yoo Si-min's politics." Five-term lawmaker Park Ji-won said, "The claim that President Lee Jae-myung has tried not to reform the prosecution over the past year is utterly groundless." <<> Inside and outside the ruling camp, some have suggested that the newly mainstreamed "New Lee Jae-myung" supporter base, which emerged after President Lee's election, and the traditional pro-Roh and pro-Moon supporter base have begun a full-scale civil war over the abolition of the prosecution's supplementary investigation power and the party convention. Yoo has previously criticized the New Lee Jae-myung supporter base, saying "they flowed in chasing after interests." Kim Eo-jun also said that day, "Wasn't it agreed to only grant the right to request supplementary investigations? Keep your promise." <<> With about a month to go until the August party convention, competition among party leadership contenders is intensifying, and the language being used against each other is becoming increasingly harsh. On the 15th, lawmaker Song Young-gil said in a radio interview regarding former leader Jung Cheong-rae's recent comments that the Democratic Party should not have fielded a candidate in the June 3 by-election for the Gyeonggi Pyeongtaek-eul National Assembly seat, calling it "the same as saying to your own son, 'I should have aborted you, but I gave birth to you.'" <<> The previous day, targeting former leader Jung, Song also said, "Just shouting 'Lee Jae-myung' a few times won't make the 'Myung-Cheong War' disappear. It's stalker level," and "(The Myung-Cheong conflict) in the old days would have been a situation where you'd have to behead traitors to suppress it." <<> Within the party, there are observations that Song's concentrated attacks on former leader Jung are intended to highlight his presence as a party leadership contender. However, there are also considerable criticisms that Song's high-level remarks could backfire by fostering "sympathy for Jung Cheong-rae" in the Honam region and elsewhere. Jung, who previously compared being attacked by multiple candidates to being ganged up on, wrote on Facebook that day, "This is too much," and "I believe the party members will protect me." (유시민씨가 15일 이재명 대통령의 ‘검찰 개혁’과 정국 운영에 대해 “매우 잘못된 판단을 하고 있다”며 “필연적인 실패의 길로 가고 있다”고 했다. 이재명 정부가 집권 2년 차에 막 접어든 상황에서 여권 인사가 ‘실패’를 언급하며 공개 비판한 것은 이례적인 일이다. 검찰 보완수사권 폐지와 8월 더불어민주당 전당대회를 앞두고 여권 내 진영 갈등이 내전 상태에 빠져들 수 있다는 전망도 나온다.)

item.title: A Democratic Stronghold, Yet... Zero Candidates from Jeonnam-Gwangju for Supreme Council Seats (민주당 텃밭인데… 전남광주 의원들 최고위원 출마 0명)
item.description:
A Democratic Stronghold, Yet... Zero Candidates from Jeonnam-Gwangju for Supreme Council Seats (민주당 텃밭인데… 전남광주 의원들 최고위원 출마 0명)

With the registration period for the Democratic Party of Korea’s August 17 national convention candidates set for the 16th–17th, as of the 15th, not a single lawmaker from the party’s traditional stronghold of South Jeolla Province and Gwangju had entered the race for the Supreme Council seats. Some lawmakers had considered running but ultimately backed out. A key party insider said, “It’s because they know they’d lose anyway.” (더불어민주당 8·17 전당대회 후보 등록(16~17일)을 앞두고 15일까지 여권 텃밭인 전남광주 의원들이 최고위원 선거에 단 한 명도 출사표를 내지 않았다. 일부 의원이 출마를 검토했지만 막판에 접었다고 한다. 민주당 핵심 관계자는 “나가봤자 떨어질 게 뻔하기 때문”이라고 했다.)

Party leadership contenders are visiting Jeonnam-Gwangju almost daily, underscoring the importance of the party’s base there. Yet, no lawmaker from Jeonnam-Gwangju is among the Supreme Council candidates. Rep. Jeong Jin-uk, a pro-Lee Jae-myung figure representing Gwangju’s Dongnam Gap district, deliberated a run but ultimately declared he would not stand. (민주당 당권 주자들은 하루가 멀다 하고 전남광주를 찾고 있다. 그만큼 이곳 당심이 중요하기 때문이다. 하지만 정작 최고위원 후보에 전남광주 의원은 없는 것이다. 광주 동남갑이 지역구인 친명계 정진욱 의원이 출마를 고민했지만 불출마를 선언했다.)

The reluctance of Jeonnam-Gwangju lawmakers to enter the race stems from a string of electoral defeats suffered by candidates from the region in recent years. After Rep. Yang Hyang-ja, then a Democratic Party member, was elected to the Supreme Council in the 2020 party convention, they faced consecutive losses. Rep. Seo Sam-seok in 2021, Rep. Song Gap-seok in 2022, and Rep. Min Hyung-bae in 2024 all ran and lost. Notably, Rep. Min topped the primary in Jeonnam-Gwangju but fell behind elsewhere, finishing 7th out of eight candidates. For this reason, when the party leader appoints two Supreme Council members, they have historically included a figure from the Honam region. Former leader Lee Jae-myung appointed Gwangju-born lawyer Im Sun-sook, while former leader Jeong Cheong-rae appointed Rep. Seo Sam-seok. <<> Political circles point to the fact that most lawmakers from Jeonnam-Gwangju are first-term representatives as a key reason for the lack of candidates. All eight lawmakers from Gwangju are currently serving their first term, while four out of ten from the South Jeolla Province district are first-term members. A party insider noted, “Jeonnam-Gwangju is sensitive to political trends, leading to a frequent turnover in every election. With changes in party leadership, they get swept away, leaving no room for Honam members to build the political weight that satisfies local party loyalists.” <<> Another analysis suggests that as the Democratic Party has become centered on the Seoul-Gyeonggi metropolitan area, elections are now driven more by factional dynamics than regional representation. A person who previously worked on a Supreme Council campaign said, “Factions concentrate votes on one or two candidates, so an ambiguous Honam candidate ends up stuck in the middle or lower ranks.” A party insider added, “Aside from former President Kim Dae-jung and former Prime Minister Lee Nak-yon, there are almost no prominent politicians from Jeonnam-Gwangju. It’s a similar situation to how it’s difficult for Honam-born politicians to become the Democratic Party’s standard-bearer, such as a presidential candidate.” (전남광주 의원들이 출사표를 내지 못하는 이유는 최근 선거에서 이 지역 출신들이 고배를 마셨기 때문이다. 2020년 전당대회에서 당시 민주당이던 양향자 의원이 최고위원으로 뽑힌 뒤 줄줄이 낙선했다. 2021년 서삼석 의원, 2022년 송갑석 의원, 2024년 민형배 의원이 도전했으나 모두 떨어졌다. 특히 민 의원은 전남광주 경선에선 1위를 했으나 다른 지역에서 밀려 8명 중 7위에 그쳤다. 이 때문에 민주당 당대표가 최고위원 2명을 지명할 때 호남 출신을 넣어왔다. 이재명 대통령은 당대표 시절 광주 출신인 임선숙 변호사를, 정청래 전 대표는 서삼석 의원을 임명했다.)

item.description:
[Episode 27] Tokyo's Skyline ([27화] 도쿄의 스카이라인)

☞ View from Episode 1 (☞ 1화부터 보기)

☞ Character Introduction (☞ 등장인물 소개)

Three months after Sariel’s successful debut, Evan transferred from the Korean branch to the Japanese branch. (사리엘의 성공적인 데뷔 3개월 후, 에반은 한국 지사에서 일본 지사로 자리를 옮겼다.)

Evan began his new journey in a 33-story mansion in Tokyo's Minato-ku, designated by the company. While scrolling on his smartphone in the living room, he looked up to see the Tokyo cityscape spread out beyond the mansion's signature floor-to-ceiling windows. The orderly roads and the forest of silver buildings seemed to hold everything in its place. (에반은 회사가 지정한 도쿄 미나토구 33층 맨션에서 새 여정을 시작했다. 거실에서 스마트폰을 스크롤링하다 고개를 들자 맨션 특유의 통유리창 너머로 도쿄 시내가 펼쳐졌다. 질서 정연하게 뻗은 도로와 은색 빌딩 숲이 모든 것을 제자리에 가둬놓은 듯했다.)

Gazing out the window, leaving the bitter taste of espresso on his tongue, Evan scrolled down his email window. (에반은 창밖을 바라보다 에스프레소의 쓴맛을 혀끝에 남긴 채, 이메일 창을 하단으로 내렸다.)

Subject: Transfer Confirmation — APAC Strategy Director, Tokyo (Subject: Transfer Confirmation — APAC Strategy Director, Tokyo)

It was the confirmation email for his promotion and transfer that HR had sent two weeks ago. (2주 전, HR이 보내준 승진 인사 확정 메일이었다.)

It wasn't that he had been chasing success over the past decade since his discharge from Iraq. The driving force behind Evan rolling on the floor of the DMZ and burning the midnight oil writing proposals in a tiny room in Pyeongtaek was his mindset to overcome the "Three-Second Ghost" through his creation, Sariel. (이라크 제대 후 지난 십여 년간 출세를 좇은 것은 아니었다. 에반이 휴전선 바닥을 뒹굴고, 평택 골방에서 밤새워 제안서를 썼던 원동력은, 사리엘이라는 작품으로 ‘3초의 망령’을 극복하려는 마음가짐이었다.)

Nevertheless, the event of a promotion was clearly a significant milestone in his life, allowing him to feel a sense of accomplishment from his work for the first time in a long while. (그럼에도 승진이라는 이벤트는 분명, 꽤 오랜만에 자신이 해온 일에 보람을 느낄 수 있는 인생의 마일스톤이었다.)

Just a few months ago, he had only been staring at the concrete walls of Camp Humphreys in Pyeongtaek, but now Tokyo's entire skyline was framed within his window. (몇 달 전까지 평택 기지의 콘크리트 벽만 보고 있었는데, 이젠 도쿄의 스카이라인이 통째로 창 안에 들어왔다.)

"Evan, look over there. You can really see Mount Fuji." (“에반, 저기 좀 봐. 후지산이 진짜 보여.”)

Irina came into the living room with a still-sleepy voice. When Evan said he had to go to Tokyo, she didn't hesitate to board the plane with him. (이리나가 잠이 덜 깬 목소리로 거실에 나왔다. 그녀는 에반이 도쿄로 가야 한다고 하자, 주저 없이 도쿄행 비행기에 같이 몸을 실었다.)

"I'm making enough money. Just come with me." (“돈은 충분히 벌고 있어. 몸만 따라와 줘.”)

That was Evan's offer, and for Irina, that one sentence was enough. (그것이 에반의 제의였고, 이리나에게는 그 말 한마디면 충분했다.)

Being an experienced bodyguard, she could find part-time work in any city, so Irina adapted quickly in Tokyo. The symbiotic relationship they had built up through London, Poland, and Pyeongtaek continued naturally into Tokyo. (숙련된 경호원은 어느 도시에서든 파트타임 일자리를 구할 수 있었기에, 이리나는 도쿄에서도 금세 적응했다. 런던과 폴란드, 평택을 거치며 쌓인 둘의 공생 관계는 도쿄까지도 자연스레 이어졌다.)

"See, I told you. I said you'd have great career success this year. Getting promoted and even coming to Japan. My app was spot on." (“거봐, 내가 뭐랬어. 올해 당신이 커리어적으로 크게 성공한다고 했잖아. 승진해서 일본으로까지 오게 되고. 내 앱이 정확했다니까.”)

Standing by the marble table with a piece of toast in her mouth, Irina began scrolling through her astrology app. With a slight smile lingering in her eyes, she swiped her thumb frantically before turning the screen towards Evan. (이리나는 대리석 식탁에 서서 토스트를 입에 문 채 점성술 앱을 훑기 시작했다. 잔웃음이 남은 눈으로 정신없이 엄지를 쓸어내리던 그녀가, 화면을 에반 쪽으로 돌렸다.)

[Today's Transit][Venus is passing through your partner's 7th House. This is the section where the orbits of the two of you come closest. Luck in love is on the rise, and your mutual dependence becomes a structure, not a weakness.][MN1] ([오늘의 트랜짓][금성이 파트너의 7하우스를 통과하고 있습니다. 두 사람의 궤도가 가장 가까워지는 구간입니다. 애정운은 상승 기류를 타고, 서로에 대한 의존은 약점이 아니라 구조가 됩니다.][MN1] )

"Did you hear that? Dependence is a structure, not a weakness. The app knows us better than we know ourselves." (“들었지? 의존은 약점이 아니라 구조래. 앱이 우리보다 우리를 잘 알아.”)

As Irina read aloud with delight, her expression froze at the next card. (기분 좋은 듯 소리 내어 읽던 이리나의 표정이 다음 카드에서 굳었다.)

[Caution: Mars enters Capricorn][The planet of action, Mars, stands cold and still at the peak of your partner's 10th House, the pinnacle of career. Shadows are cast alongside the place of achievement. Accidents occur on familiar paths, from unexpected angles.][MN2] ([주의: 화성, 염소자리 진입][행동의 행성 화성이 파트너의 10하우스, 커리어의 정점 위에서 차갑게 멈춥니다. 성취의 자리에는 그림자가 함께 배치됩니다. 사고는 익숙한 동선에서, 예상하지 못한 각도로 찾아옵니다.][MN2] )

"Evan... it says there could be an unexpected accident?" (“에반… 예상치 못한 사고가 날 수 있다는데?”)

Evan unconsciously rubbed his left fingertips. (에반은 무의식적으로 왼손 손가락 끝을 만지작거렸다.)

"My life is decided by algorithms. Not by the positions of stars." (“내 인생은 알고리즘이 결정해. 별자리 위치가 아니라.”)

"There are things algorithms can't catch," Irina's voice lost its playfulness. "Unexpected accidents can happen anytime, not just from fortune telling. What's scarier than that is you freezing up again at that critical moment when I'm not there." (“알고리즘이 못 잡는 것도 있어.” 이리나의 목소리에서 장난기가 빠졌다. “예상치 못한 사고는 점괘가 아니어도 언제든 일어나. 그것보다 무서운 건, 내가 없을 때 당신이 그 찰나에 또 멈춰버리는 거야.”)

Evan adjusted his tie and answered nonchalantly, but Irina's intuition picked up on a strange chill. She added with a pout. (에반은 넥타이를 매만지며 심드렁하게 대답했지만, 이리나의 직관은 묘한 한기를 잡아냈다. 그녀가 뾰루퉁한 표정으로 덧붙였다.)

"Evan, there's no harm in being careful." (“에반, 조심해서 나쁠 건 없잖아.”)

"Got it. I'll be careful." (“알겠어. 조심할게.”)

"I'm recording that." (“그 말 녹음해둔다.”)

Leaving Irina's sharp-tongued joke behind, Evan headed out for his first day of work. (이리나의 뼈 있는 농담을 뒤로하고 에반은 첫 출근길에 올랐다.)

His destination was Toranomon, not far from the mansion. An area dense with Tokyo's wealthy, large law firms, and global corporations. Dudal Japan occupied an entire floor of the tallest building there. The atmosphere was completely different from the fortress-like office in Pyeongtaek. (목적지는 맨션에서 멀지 않은 토라노몬이었다. 도쿄의 부유층과 대형 로펌, 글로벌 기업들이 밀집한 구역. 듀다엘 재팬은 그곳에서도 가장 높은 빌딩 한 층을 통째로 사용했다. 평택의 군사 요새 같은 사무실과는 공기부터 달랐다.)

"Evan Yoon? So you're the famous APAC strategy lead!" (“에반 윤? 당신이 그 유명한 APAC 전략 담당자!”)

Mark, the American Vice President of the Japan branch, lightly tapped Evan's shoulder as he guided him around the office. There was a characteristic, manufactured, energetic vibe in his gestures. (일본 지사의 미국인 부지사장 마크가 에반의 어깨를 가볍게 치며 사무실을 안내했다. 미국인 특유의 가공된 활기찬 기운이 몸짓에서 느껴졌다.)

"This is the break room, over there is the analysis team. Let me know if you have any questions." (“여기는 휴게실, 저쪽은 분석팀. 궁금한 거 있으면 언제든 말해.”)

As Evan passed by, the Japanese employees didn't take their eyes off their monitors. Mark didn't seem to notice. Only the sound of keyboards filled the tense silence. Mark was someone who had long given up on reading the room. (에반이 지나가는 동안 일본인 직원들은 모니터에서 눈을 떼지 않았다. 마크는 눈치채지 못하는 것 같았다. 키보드 소리만이 팽팽한 정적을 메웠다. 마크는 오래전에 분위기 파악을 포기한 사람이었다.)

Evan felt it as a wall. (에반은 그것을 벽으로 느꼈다.)

Instead of Sariel's blue interface, the local employees' monitors were full of Excel sheets and mechanical drawings reviewing compatibility with local Japanese vendors. Though the matrix organization structure mixed employees of various nationalities, the Japanese staff stayed strictly within their inner circle. They seemed to view Evan not as a technical expert, but as a monitor sent from headquarters. (현지 직원들의 모니터에는 사리엘의 파란색 인터페이스 대신, 일본 로컬 업체들과의 호환성을 검토하는 엑셀 시트와 기계 도면이 가득했다. 매트릭스 조직이라는 이름 아래 여러 국적의 직원을 섞어 놓았지만, 일본 직원들은 철저하게 자신들의 이너 서클 안에 머물렀다. 에반을 기술 전문가가 아니라 본사에서 보낸 감시자로 여기는 듯했다.)

"Alright, that's the end of the office tour. The Branch Manager wants to see you, so head over there." (“자 그럼 사무실 소개는 이걸로 끝났고, 지사장님이 보자니까 저기로 가면 돼.”)

Evan headed to the office of Kenji Tanaka, the Branch Manager of Dudal Japan. It was an executive office with a panoramic view of Tokyo Tower. Tanaka gestured towards the reception sofa. (에반은 듀다엘 일본 지사장 다나카 켄지의 방으로 향했다. 도쿄타워가 한눈에 보이는 임원실이었다. 다나카가 응접 소파를 손바닥으로 가리켰다.)

"Team Lead Evan, I'll be honest with you. The Japanese government is not happy." (“에반 팀장, 솔직히 말할게요. 일본 정부는 곤란해하고 있어요.”)

Tanaka started talking business without any preamble. Speaking in fluent English, he didn't seem like the typical Japanese boss. (다나카는 다짜고짜 일 얘기부터 시작했다. 유창한 영어로 말하는 것이 전형적인 일본인 상사는 아닌 것 같았다.)

"The problem is that while they inwardly acknowledge Sariel's performance, their pride is hurt. There's significant resistance to belatedly adopting a system that Korea introduced first." (“사리엘의 성능은 내심 인정하면서도 자존심에 상처를 입은 게 문제예요. 한국이 먼저 도입한 시스템을 뒤늦게 따라가는 데 대한 거부감이 상당하다는 말이에요.”)

"After Sariel's first public demonstration last time?" (“지난번 사리엘 첫 공개 이후요?”)

"The Japanese media went crazy back then. While the Chief Cabinet Secretary just kept repeating 'under review,' Korea had already disclosed the coordinates. The government lost face internally." (“그때 일본 언론이 뒤집어졌으니까. 관방장관이 ‘분석 중’만 반복하는 사이 한국은 좌표까지 공개했잖아. 정부 내부에서 체면이 구겨진 거죠.”)

Tanaka took a gulp of the Pepsi sitting on his desk. (다나카가 탁상에 놓인 펩시를 한 모금 들이켰다.)

"Internally, they're using doubts about whether 'Korean-style optimization' fits the Japanese archipelago as a shield. Questioning whether an algorithm tuned for mountainous terrain can handle the noise generated by the Pacific's complex coastline and tens of thousands of islands." (“내부적으로는 ‘한국형 최적화’가 일본 열도에도 맞느냐는 의구심을 방패로 쓰고 있어요. 산악 지형에 맞춰진 알고리즘이 태평양의 복잡한 해안선과 수만 개의 섬에서 발생할 노이즈를 감당할 수 있겠느냐는 거죠.”)

"That's technically manageable. Past marine environment simulations have already..." (“그건 기술적으로 대응 가능합니다. 과거 해양 환경 시뮬레이션을 이미…")

"Mm... technically, that's not the issue," Tanaka cut Evan off. "Ultimately, it's a domestic political problem." (“음… 정확히는 기술 문제가 아니에요.” 다나카가 에반의 말을 잘랐다. “결국 국내 정치 문제인 거죠.”)

Tanaka gave a wry smile. (다나카가 쓴웃음을 지었다.)

"They want Sariel to become Japan's digital lighthouse in Yonaguni and Okinawa, but they fear Chinese retaliation. They've seen what happened to Korea. So, they've presented us with an offset trade bill." (“사리엘이 요나구니와 오키나와에서 일본의 디지털 등대가 되어주길 바라면서도, 중국의 보복은 두려워해요. 한국이 당한 꼴을 봤으니까. 그러면서 우리에겐 절충 교역이라는 청구서를 내밀었어요.”)

Offset trade. A transaction method where the buyer requires the seller to make reciprocal purchases or local investments equivalent to the contract value. (절충 교역. 무기를 사주는 대가로 비슷한 금액의 무기를 되사거나 현지 투자를 요구하는 거래 방식이다.)

But Japan's situation was a bit more complicated. (하지만 일본은 사정이 조금 더 복잡했다.)

"The Japanese government is apparently demanding Shirakawa Heavy Industries as a partner." (“일본 정부는 파트너로 시라카와 중공업을 요구하고 있다고 하네요.”)

Tanaka's voice dropped. (다나카의 목소리가 낮아졌다.)

"Shirakawa isn't just a company. It's the final stop for retired Ministry of Defense officials parachuting into new jobs—what they call 'amakudari.' They were a giant that sustained the empire's pride during WWII, building battleships and fighter planes, but were effectively shrunk into a local company by Article 9 of the Peace Constitution. They dream of a global resurgence through deregulation, but internal corruption and inefficiency make them both impossible to discard and difficult to keep for the Japanese government—a real white elephant." (“시라카와는 단순한 기업이 아니에요. 방위성 퇴직 관료들이 재취업하는 낙하산의 종착역, 흔히들 아마쿠다리라고 부르죠. 2차 대전 당시 전함과 전투기를 만들며 제국의 자존심을 지탱했던 거인인데, 평화헌법 9조에 묶여 로컬 기업으로 쪼그라들었다고 봐야죠. 규제 완화로 글로벌 시장 재도약을 꿈꾸고 있지만, 내부 부패와 비효율로 일본 정부에는 버릴 수도 안고 갈 수도 없는 계륵이라고나 할까요.”)

"Similar to Korea's Taesan Defense, yet different." (“한국의 태산디펜스와 비슷하면서도 다르군요.”)

Tanaka nodded. (다나카가 고개를 끄덕였다.)

"Shirakawa's technological level is still higher, but they lost their drive and will for expansion at some point. Only the political connections survived. The Japanese government's plan might be to use Sariel as an oxygen tank for Shirakawa." (“시라카와 쪽이 아직 기술력 수준은 더 높지만, 어느 시점에서 확장의 동력과 의지를 잃었어요. 정치적 연줄만 살아남은 거죠. 일본 정부는 사리엘을 시라카와의 산소 호흡기로 쓰겠다는 복안이 아닐까요.”)

"For now, I'll review the situation." (“일단, 상황을 검토해 보겠습니다.”)

Evan returned to his desk. A package from West Coast Labs had been delivered to one side of his desk. A note attached said it was a Sariel-compatible smartglass prototype for field testing. (에반은 자리로 돌아왔다. 책상 한쪽에 웨스트코스트랩에서 보낸 소포가 배달됐다. 사리엘 연동형 스마트글라스 시제품, 필드 테스트용이라는 메모가 붙어 있었다.)

Just as he was about to open the package, his iPhone vibrated. It was a video meeting request from Jeff. Jeff had also just been promoted, based on the Sariel Korea deployment success, to Managing Director of the Global Strategy Team at the Virginia headquarters. (소포를 뜯으려던 순간, 아이폰이 진동했다. 제프의 화상 미팅 요청이었다. 사리엘 한국 도입을 성과로 인정받아 버지니아 본사의 글로벌 전략팀 매니징 디렉터로 같이 막 승진했던 터였다.)

"Evan, long time no see. Like the Tokyo scenery?" (“에반, 오랜만이야. 도쿄 풍경이 좋나?”)

"Yes. What's the matter?" (“예, 용건은 무엇인지요.”)

"You're going to be incredibly busy from now on." (“앞으로 엄청 바빠질 거야.”)

Jeff's voice on the screen was a pitch higher than during his time in Korea. It felt like a degree of arrogance had risen along with the promotion. (화면 속 제프의 목소리는 한국 시절보다 무언가 한 톤 더 올라갔다. 직급이 올라간 만큼 거드름도 한층 더 올라간 느낌이었다.)

"The company didn't send you to Tokyo to enjoy sushi. The will of HQ is to enmesh all of Asia in Sariel's network." (“회사가 당신을 도쿄로 보낸 건, 거기서 스시나 즐기라는 뜻이 아니야. 아시아 전체를 사리엘의 그물망에 넣으라는 게 본사의 의지야.”)

"The complicated situation with the Japanese government needs to be sorted out first..." (“일본 정부 쪽 복잡한 상황을 먼저 정리해야…”)

"Japan can't avoid buying it anyway. Don't sweat it too much," Jeff cut in. "A defense expo is coming up soon in Manila. I need you to manage our booth there." (“일본은 어차피 안 사고는 못 배겨. 너무 힘 빼지 마.” 제프가 잘랐다. “조만간 마닐라에서 방산 전시회가 열리는데, 거기서 부스 운영 맡아줘.”)

"Manila?" (“마닐라요?”)

"What, don't like business trips to 'developing countries'?" (“왜, 후진국 출장은 싫어?”)

"No, sir. I'll prepare." (“아뇨. 준비하겠습니다.”)

"The core of this trip isn't just Japan, it's a sales strategy targeting even the Philippine military. A big picture tying together the entire Asia-Pacific region. Directives from top management." (“이번 출장의 핵심은 일본이 아니라 필리핀 군까지 염두에 둔 세일즈 전략이야. 아시아-태평양 전체를 묶는 큰 그림. 경영진의 지시야.”)

Jeff lifted the rim of his glasses perched on his nose as he uttered the phrase 'directives from top management.' (제프는 경영진의 지시라는 단어를 내뱉으면서 코 끝에 얹힌 안경테를 치켜세웠다.)

Various discussions followed, and the video conference ended after an hour. Evan closed his laptop and left the office. (이런저런 얘기가 이어지며 화상 회의는 1시간 만에 끝났다. 에반은 노트북을 덮고 사무실을 나섰다.)

Beyond the clear Tokyo sky, a tropical depression began to move northward from the south. (도쿄의 맑은 하늘 너머, 남쪽에서 열대 저기압이 북상하기 시작했다.)

item.title: Former Navy Secretary: "Pursued Another US Shipyard Project with Hanwha During Tenure, Beyond Philadelphia" (前해군장관 “재임 중 한화와 필리 外 또 다른 美조선소 사업 추진”)
item.description:
Former Navy Secretary: "Pursued Another US Shipyard Project with Hanwha During Tenure, Beyond Philadelphia" (前해군장관 “재임 중 한화와 필리 外 또 다른 美조선소 사업 추진”)

Former U.S. Navy Secretary John Phelan stated on the 15th, "The United States needs new shipyards and trained personnel," adding, "We sought to pursue another shipyard project in cooperation with Hanwha, which has achieved excellent results by acquiring the Philadelphia shipyard. While I cannot disclose the name, the goal was to have Hanwha expand its operations in the U.S. and play a greater role in transferring its technology and expertise to America." Phelan, a billionaire businessman and close associate of President Donald Trump, served as Navy Secretary from March 2025 to April this year, leading efforts to revive the U.S. shipbuilding industry and engaging in U.S.-Korea shipbuilding cooperation. <<> Speaking at the Aspen Security Forum (ASF) held in Aspen, Colorado, on the same day, Phelan responded to a question about why countries like South Korea can build more ships than the U.S., saying, "South Korea has adopted more modern technologies, such as robotics." Phelan visited South Korea last April and toured HD Hyundai Heavy Industries' Ulsan shipyard. He noted, "When a welder presses a button, someone brings components, so they can just keep welding, whereas the U.S. lacks such a system," and "Even in the nuclear submarine construction site in Connecticut, digital twin technology was not applied to the design, so we had to introduce it." He also remarked on the shipbuilding industry, saying, "There's a characteristic that the more ships you build, the faster the work becomes," and "The fact that people in a village have been working for five generations is something to learn from South Korea and Japan." <<> Phelan said, "China is currently building over 1,700 ships annually, while the U.S. builds only five. The gap is widening. China has a shipyard large enough to fit all of America's shipyards, which is absurd." During his tenure, he actively pursued U.S.-Korea shipbuilding cooperation and indicated that he explored Hanwha's acquisition of additional shipyards in the U.S. Michael Coulter, CEO of Hanwha Defense USA, had stated in January this year that the Philadelphia shipyard, with only two docks, could not meet manufacturing demand, saying, "We are reviewing options to expand production capacity and storage space." Phelan also shared, "There were areas where we were somewhat lacking, so we also considered building parts of the hull in other countries or regions." <<> Trump is known to have encouraged Phelan to revive the shipbuilding industry, even showing him pictures of ships in the early morning. Phelan noted, "Professional personnel like welders and electricians are things that artificial intelligence (AI) cannot solve or replace," and argued for fairer wages to attract such workers. He also said, "The Navy fails to leverage any purchasing scale advantages in contract work, lacking business common sense, so there were really many things that needed improvement." Stepping down abruptly in April this year, he remarked, "Entering an organization like the Pentagon, which is extremely risk-averse, and insisting on taking risks inevitably ruffles a lot of people's feathers and makes them uneasy," but added, "I may have pushed too hard, but I have no regrets about what I did as Navy Secretary." <<> <<> ◇ ☞Aspen Institute <<> The Aspen Institute is a nonprofit organization founded in 1949 by American businessman Walter Paepcke in Aspen, Colorado. Originally from Chicago, Paepcke was inspired by Aspen's natural scenery and conceived the idea for world leaders to step away from their routines and engage in discussions. Its mission is "to solve the most important challenges facing the United States and the world through dialogue and leadership." It aims to be a bipartisan facilitator that steps back from political polarization to convene diverse participants for discussion. Over 30 programs operate independently in fields such as economics, education, and the environment. Since 2010, it has held the annual Aspen Security Forum, where global diplomacy and security experts discuss domestic and international issues. (존 펠런 전 미 해군 장관은 15일 “미국은 새로운 조선소와 훈련된 인력이 필요하다”며 “필라델피아 조선소를 인수해 훌륭한 성과를 내고 있는 한화와 협력해 또 다른 조선소 사업을 추진하려 했다. 이름은 밝힐 수 없으나 한화가 미국 내 사업을 확장하고, 그들이 가진 기술과 노하우를 미국으로 이전하는 데 더 많은 역할을 하도록 만들게 하는 것이었다”고 했다. 억만장자 사업가 출신이자 도널드 트럼프 대통령의 측근인 펠런은 2025년 3월부터 올해 4월까지 해군 장관을 지내며 미국의 조선업 부활을 주도하고 한미 조선 협력에도 관여해 온 인물이다.)
